standard_prerequisites.name: Units of an integral finite type algebra over an algebraically closed field
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides finite generation of the unit groups of the irreducible components modulo constants.

core_obligations: Write X as the union of its irreducible components and use the integral finite type case to get that each O(X_i)^*/k^* is finitely generated (proof lines 5297-5299).

Analyse the kernel of the map O(X)^* -> product of O(X_i)^*/k^*: a unit in the kernel restricts to an element lambda_i of k on each component, and restricting to a nonempty intersection X_i cap X_j forces lambda_i = lambda_j (proof lines 5300-5308).

Use connectedness of X to conclude that all the lambda_i agree, so the kernel is exactly k^*, and identify O(X)^*/k^* with a subgroup of a product of finitely many finitely generated abelian groups (proof lines 5309-5315).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the irreducible components by a subgroup argument.
Show the kernel of the restriction map is the constants.
Use connectedness to propagate the constant across components.
Conclude finite generation from the finite product.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that O^*(X)/k^* is finitely generated for a connected reduced scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field with finitely many irreducible components. The proof writes X as the union of its components, uses the integral finite-type case to get finite generation of each O(X_i)^*/k^*, and then analyses the kernel of the natural map O(X)^* -> product of O(X_i)^*/k^*: a unit in the kernel restricts to a constant on each component, and restricting to nonempty pairwise intersections forces those constants to agree, while connectedness of X forces all of them to agree, so the kernel is exactly k^* (proof lines 5297-5310). This exhibits O(X)^*/k^* as a subgroup of a product of finitely many finitely generated abelian groups, giving the result (proof lines 5311-5315). H2: the kernel analysis via connectedness is the substance.
